Attack on Titan
An absolute masterpiece. The storytelling is unparalleled, the animation during titan battles is breathtaking and the plot twists completely redefine the entire series. Season 4 is peak anime.
Attack on Titan
Brilliant world-building and morally complex characters. Eren Yeager has one of the most shocking character arcs I have ever seen in fiction. The final season had me emotional throughout.
Attack on Titan
The lore is astonishing. Every mystery introduced in season one pays off brilliantly. The animation by MAPPA in the final arc is stunning. Highly recommended.
Attack on Titan
Fantastic anime with incredible action sequences. The story gets very dark and political in later seasons but that is what makes it special. Took me two watches to fully appreciate it.
Attack on Titan
The first two seasons were amazing but the pacing slows down noticeably. Too much talking and political drama replaced the exciting titan battles I loved.
Attack on Titan
The ending was deeply disappointing and divisive. After years of build-up the conclusion felt rushed and unsatisfying. The plot holes in the final arc ruined it for me.
Attack on Titan
One of the most thoughtfully written stories in anime. The themes of freedom war and cycle of hatred are handled with incredible nuance. Absolutely deserves its legendary status.
Attack on Titan
Overhyped in my opinion. The story becomes unnecessarily complicated in later arcs and loses the horror atmosphere that made the first season so compelling.
Attack on Titan
Perfect in every way. Voice acting, soundtrack, animation and story all top tier. Yoko Shinomura and Hiroyuki Sawano delivered legendary OSTs. Watch it immediately.
Attack on Titan
Very good anime overall but the manga ending controversy carries over somewhat. Still the animation and character development make it worth every episode.
Death Note
The greatest psychological thriller in anime. The cat and mouse game between Light and L is the most gripping thing I have ever watched. Every episode left me desperate for the next.
Death Note
Exceptional writing and brilliant characters. Light Yagami is a fascinating villain protagonist and L is one of the most iconic anime characters ever created.
Death Note
Incredible first half followed by a slightly weaker second half after a major character exits. Still a must-watch for anyone interested in psychological anime.
Death Note
The first arc was perfect but the second half with Near and Mello felt like a pale imitation. Wish it had ended earlier for a more satisfying conclusion.
Death Note
Masterpiece storytelling. The internal monologues show us exactly how a genius mind calculates every move. Light and L are the best rivalry in anime history.
Death Note
Light is thoroughly unlikeable which makes it hard to enjoy. Three quarters of the show is just him talking to himself while monologuing endlessly.
Death Note
One of the most binge-worthy anime ever made. The tension never lets up and the moral questions it raises about justice and power are genuinely thought-provoking.
Death Note
Brilliant concept executed well. The later arcs are weaker but the core premise and execution in the first arc is some of the best writing in all of anime.
Death Note
The opening credits set the tone perfectly. Light Yagami descending into madness while believing he is righteous is haunting and compelling. Absolute classic.
Death Note
Could not get past how pretentious the second half felt. Near was a poor substitute for L and the finale felt anticlimactic compared to the brilliance of the early episodes.
Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood
The greatest anime ever made. Perfect pacing, incredible characters, emotional depth and a satisfying ending that ties every thread together beautifully.
Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood
I cried multiple times. Every character gets meaningful development. The themes of sacrifice family and the cost of ambition are handled perfectly. A benchmark for the medium.
Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood
Exceptional storytelling with a cast of genuinely memorable characters. Roy Mustang and Edward Elric are among the best protagonists in anime. Highly recommended.
Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood
Brilliant anime with minor pacing issues in the middle arcs. The early episodes rush content familiar from the 2003 series but the original content is outstanding.
Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood
Maes Hughes arc hit me harder than anything in fiction. The emotional punches land perfectly because the show takes time to make you genuinely care. Flawless experience.
Fullmetal Alchemist Brotherhood
Very good but slightly overrated in my view. The ending felt a bit rushed and some villains were underdeveloped. Still one of the better anime I have completed.
Demon Slayer
Ufotable produces the most visually stunning animation in the industry and Demon Slayer is their crowning achievement. The Water Breathing sequences are breathtaking artwork.
Demon Slayer
Tanjiro is one of the most wholesome and emotionally resonant protagonists in recent anime. His kindness even towards demons makes this stand apart from other shonen series.
Demon Slayer
Gorgeous animation that pushes what TV anime can look like. The Mugen Train arc made me sob uncontrollably. Rengoku is one of the best anime characters in years.
Demon Slayer
Visually stunning but narratively thin. The story is fairly straightforward and the villains feel shallow. Great spectacle but lacks the writing depth of its peers.
Demon Slayer
The Entertainment District arc is peak anime action. Tengen Uzui and the Sound Breathing sequences against Daki and Gyutaro are the most beautifully animated fights I have seen.
Demon Slayer
Overrated due to animation budget. The story is predictable shonen formula and Zenitsu screaming every episode becomes unbearable quickly. All style no substance.
Demon Slayer
The combination of Hinokami Kagura animation with the Fate soundtrack creates moments of genuine transcendence in anime. Demon Slayer deserves every award it receives.
Steins;Gate
The greatest science fiction anime ever created. The time travel mechanics are internally consistent and the emotional payoff of the final arc destroyed me emotionally.
Steins;Gate
Slow start but once it clicks around episode eight the show becomes completely unmissable. Okabe is one of the most complex and human protagonists in all of anime.
Steins;Gate
Brilliant writing that rewards patient viewers. The first half builds the world carefully and the second half uses every established detail to devastating emotional effect.
Steins;Gate
Excellent anime but the slow opening episodes almost made me drop it. Persevere because the payoff is absolutely worth it. El Psy Kongroo.
Steins;Gate
No anime has made me feel as much as Steins Gate. The time loop mechanics are handled with a precision and heart that is simply unmatched in the genre.
Steins;Gate
The science is interesting but the harem anime tropes in the first half are distracting and dated. Kurisu is a great character but the supporting cast feels underdeveloped.
Naruto
The original Naruto is a coming of age story told beautifully. The themes of perseverance and belonging resonated deeply with me. Pain arc is legendary storytelling.
Naruto
The anime itself is wonderful but the excessive filler content in Naruto Shippuden makes it nearly impossible to recommend. Over two hundred filler episodes is inexcusable.
Naruto
Naruto Uzumaki is one of the most inspiring protagonists in anime. His journey from a lonely outcast to a beloved hero is genuinely moving despite the filler padding.
Naruto
Too much filler destroyed the pacing entirely. The original manga story is excellent but the anime adaptation wastes your time constantly with irrelevant side stories.
Naruto
Iconic anime that defined a generation. The fight choreography and jutsus are creative and the emotional stakes feel real. Worth watching the filler-free cut.
Naruto
Classic shonen with excellent highs. The Valley of the End battle between Naruto and Sasuke in the original series is still one of the most emotionally resonant fights ever.
One Piece
The greatest adventure story ever told across any medium. Eiichiro Oda has created a world so rich and characters so beloved that it is unmatched in scope and heart.
One Piece
Marineford arc is the greatest sequence of events in all of anime. Oda planted seeds for these events hundreds of episodes earlier. The craftsmanship is extraordinary.
One Piece
Incredible story but the anime pacing is notoriously slow with constant flashbacks and speed frames. Highly recommend the manga or watching at double speed.
One Piece
The Strawhats are the most lovable crew in anime. Every arc introduces worlds so creative and emotional that it is impossible not to become attached.
One Piece
Too long to comfortably recommend. The story is amazing but asking someone to commit to over a thousand episodes is unrealistic. Start with the manga instead.
One Piece
Thriller Bark Water 7 Dressrosa Wano. Every arc outdoes the previous one. Oda is a once in a generation creative genius and One Piece is his magnum opus.
Neon Genesis Evangelion
A profound psychological deconstruction of the mech genre that doubles as a meditation on depression loneliness and the human need for connection. Changed anime forever.
Neon Genesis Evangelion
Deeply influential and impressively ambitious. The character psychology is years ahead of its time but the budget limitations and abstract ending divide audiences.
Neon Genesis Evangelion
I appreciate what Evangelion tried to do more than what it actually delivered. The last two episodes feel like an excuse for the budget limitations.
Neon Genesis Evangelion
End of Evangelion is one of the most audacious things ever put on screen. Terrifying beautiful and deeply moving. Anno created something genuinely unique.
Neon Genesis Evangelion
Too obtuse and self-indulgent in its symbolism. The psychological deconstruction is interesting but the show wallows in misery without providing satisfying resolution.
Hunter x Hunter
The Chimera Ant arc is the greatest extended story arc in all of manga and anime. Togashi deconstructs shonen genre conventions with unparalleled intelligence and depth.
Hunter x Hunter
Killua and Gon have the most emotionally resonant friendship in anime. The Chimera Ant arc showing Gon descending into rage is terrifying and heartbreaking in equal measure.
Hunter x Hunter
Exceptional anime that consistently subverts expectations. The power system Nen is the most creative and strategically rich system in the shonen genre.
Hunter x Hunter
Outstanding in almost every way. The Yorknew City arc is perfect crime thriller anime. Would be a ten but the abrupt hiatus ending is deeply frustrating.
Hunter x Hunter
Great anime hampered by Togashi hiatus issues affecting the anime adaptation. The story and characters are superb but the journey to completion feels uncertain.
My Hero Academia
The best modern shonen series for newcomers to anime. Deku growth is inspiring and All Might remains one of the greatest mentor figures in the genre.
My Hero Academia
Solid enjoyable anime with likeable characters and creative Quirk designs. The hero society worldbuilding is interesting but the villains feel underdeveloped early on.
My Hero Academia
Good but overhyped. The formula is very standard shonen and it takes many seasons before the story develops real weight. Bakugo redemption arc took way too long.
My Hero Academia
Season 5 My Villain Academia arc completely elevated the series. Shigaraki character development is exceptional and the League of Villains became truly compelling.
My Hero Academia
Mid by the later seasons. Started strong but the constant power-up cycles and tournament arc formula make it feel repetitive. The final war arc divided the fanbase.
Cowboy Bebop
A timeless masterpiece. The jazz-noir aesthetic, Yoko Kanno legendary soundtrack, and Spike Spiegel tragic story create something that transcends the anime medium.
Cowboy Bebop
See you space cowboy. One of the most stylistically cohesive artistic visions ever committed to animation. Every episode is a self-contained gem of storytelling.
Cowboy Bebop
The episodic format allows incredible variety while the overarching Spike and Vicious storyline provides emotional weight. The finale is genuinely heartbreaking.
Cowboy Bebop
Impeccably cool and brilliantly written. The character of Spike Spiegel belongs in conversations about the greatest protagonists in all of fiction.
Cowboy Bebop
Very stylish but the episodic nature means some episodes are brilliant and others feel disposable. Appreciated intellectually more than emotionally for me personally.
Your Lie in April
The most emotionally devastating anime I have ever watched. The classical music sequences are stunning and Kaori story destroyed me completely. Absolute masterpiece.
Your Lie in April
Beautiful heartbreaking and musically magnificent. The animation of piano and violin performances is some of the finest technical work in anime. Cried for hours.
Your Lie in April
Exceptional emotional anime. The ending is one of the most moving finales I have seen anywhere. Kaori is one of the most memorable characters in romance anime.
Your Lie in April
Gorgeously animated but the melodrama becomes overwhelming. The supporting characters feel like plot devices and some of the dialogue is painfully on the nose.
Your Lie in April
This anime made me appreciate classical music genuinely for the first time. Simultaneously beautiful and unbearably sad. Mandatory viewing for romance anime fans.
Dragon Ball Z
The foundational shonen anime that defined the genre for an entire generation worldwide. The Freeza saga and Cell saga remain iconic despite their age.
Dragon Ball Z
Nostalgia plays a huge role but the power level inflation and filler battles become tedious. Still enormously fun and the Super Saiyan transformations remain iconic.
Dragon Ball Z
Goku and Vegeta rivalry is one of the best in fiction. The emotional beats land despite the simple storytelling. Gohan vs Cell is still incredible to watch.
Dragon Ball Z
The pacing is legendary in how bad it is. Characters power up for entire episodes. The manga version is much tighter. Still holds cultural importance though.
Dragon Ball Z
The battle of Namek is genuinely exciting and Vegeta arc from villain to antihero is handled surprisingly well. Timeless entry in the shonen canon.
Violet Evergarden
The most beautiful anime I have ever seen in terms of both animation and emotional storytelling. Every letter-writing episode is a contained masterpiece of human connection.
Violet Evergarden
Kyoto Animation at their absolute peak. The attention to detail the lighting the way emotions are conveyed through movement. This is art in its truest form.
Violet Evergarden
Episode ten is quite possibly the single greatest episode of television anime ever made. I have watched it three times and wept every single time without fail.
Violet Evergarden
Visually breathtaking with deeply moving episodic stories. Violet character growth is handled with incredible patience and nuance across the series.
Violet Evergarden
Stunningly beautiful but tonally inconsistent. Some episodes hit incredibly hard while others feel like they are trying too hard to manufacture emotion artificially.
Code Geass
The greatest anime ending ever. Lelouch final gambit is one of the most brilliant and emotionally devastating conclusions in all of fiction. Perfect.
Code Geass
Lelouch is the ultimate antihero. His strategic genius combined with his genuine love for his sister creates a fascinating internal conflict across two magnificent seasons.
Code Geass
Brilliantly plotted political mech anime. The cliffhangers are legendary and every episode makes you desperate for the next. The finale is absolute perfection.
Code Geass
The first season is excellent but R2 gets increasingly absurd with its plot developments. The ending saves the second season from outright mediocrity.
Code Geass
All hail Britannia. The Zero Requiem is the most satisfying ending to an anime series I have encountered. Lelouch deserves his place as one of the greatest protagonists.
Vinland Saga
The greatest Viking epic committed to any medium. Askeladd is the most complex and compelling antagonist in recent anime memory. Season one is a perfect work.
Vinland Saga
Season two slower farm arc is a brave narrative choice that pays off magnificently. The pacifism arc is one of the most thoughtful explorations of trauma in anime.
Vinland Saga
Brutal intelligent and emotionally rich. The animation handles both quiet character moments and explosive battle sequences with equal mastery throughout.
Vinland Saga
Excellent but the farm arc in season two requires patience that not all viewers will have. Those who stay are rewarded with some of the best character writing in anime.
Vinland Saga
Askeladd final scene in season one is one of the most powerful single moments in anime history. Everything Vinland Saga does narratively is done with intention and care.
Anohana
Destroyed me emotionally. The way childhood grief and guilt fracture friendships is handled with extraordinary empathy. The finale is cathartic in the most painful way.
Anohana
Short but devastatingly effective. Menma is one of the most lovable characters in anime and her story made me cry more than almost anything else I have watched.
Anohana
A genuinely moving short series about loss and unresolved feelings. The supernatural framing works beautifully to explore how grief affects different people differently.
Anohana
The emotional manipulation feels calculated and the supernatural premise strains credibility. Some character reactions feel exaggerated for dramatic effect.
Tokyo Revengers
Fun time-travel delinquent anime with genuinely likeable characters. Mikey is one of the coolest characters in recent shonen. The stakes feel real and urgent.
Tokyo Revengers
The time travel mechanics become increasingly inconsistent and the manga ending disappointed heavily. The first arc is compelling but later seasons lose the thread.
Tokyo Revengers
Entertaining but shallow. Good fight scenes and an engaging premise but the constant timeline resets undermine emotional investment in the consequences.
Tokyo Revengers
The Toman arc is some genuinely gripping anime. Mikey charisma is off the charts and the gang dynamics are well portrayed. More consistent than its reputation suggests.
Sword Art Online
The Aincrad arc is genuinely exciting trapped-in-a-game storytelling. The drop in quality after the first arc is noticeable but the original premise is still compelling.
Sword Art Online
The second arc completely abandons what made the first interesting. Kirito becomes an insufferable wish-fulfillment protagonist and the writing quality falls off a cliff.
Sword Art Online
Much more enjoyable than its reputation. Kirito and Asuna relationship in the first arc is genuinely sweet and the stakes of the death game are well established.
Sword Art Online
The Fairy Dance arc is one of the worst pieces of anime writing I have encountered. The treatment of female characters is regressive and the villain is cartoonishly evil.
Sword Art Online
Alicization arc completely redeemed the franchise. The artificial intelligence worldbuilding is genuinely interesting and Eugeo is a far better character than Kirito.
Toradora
The greatest romance anime ever made. Taiga and Ryuuji have one of the most believable and emotionally earned relationships in all of fiction. The Christmas episode destroyed me completely.
Toradora
Taiga Aisaka is one of the most iconic characters in romance anime. Her development from an aggressive loner to someone capable of genuine vulnerability is masterfully written across the series.
Toradora
The finale is one of the most satisfying and emotionally resonant conclusions in anime. Every scene in the final arc lands with incredible weight because the show took time to build real characters.
Toradora
Genuinely funny and deeply moving in equal measure. The supporting cast especially Ami Kawashima adds unexpected depth to what could have been a simple romantic comedy.
Toradora
Excellent romance anime that takes time to find its footing. The early episodes lean heavily on comedy tropes but the emotional payoff in the second half is exceptional and well worth the wait.
Toradora

One of the rare romance anime where I genuinely could not predict how it would end. The chemistry between the two leads feels completely natural and the writing never takes the easy emotional shortcut.
Clannad After Story
The most emotionally devastating piece of media I have ever consumed across any format. Clannad After Story broke me completely and I am grateful for every second of the experience.
Clannad After Story

Nothing in anime has come close to making me feel what After Story made me feel. The family arc is profound and the themes of grief love and resilience are handled with extraordinary care and honesty.
Clannad After Story
Tomoya and Nagisa have the most beautiful and heartbreaking love story in anime. After Story earns every single tear it produces through patient and genuine character development.
Clannad After Story
The transition from the lighthearted original Clannad to the devastating adult drama of After Story is one of the most impressive tonal shifts in anime. Essential viewing for any fan of the medium.
Clannad After Story
Requires watching the original Clannad first but the emotional payoff of After Story makes every moment of setup worth it. The soundtrack by Jun Maeda amplifies every scene to an unbearable degree.
Clannad After Story
Undeniably powerful in its emotional moments but some of the supernatural elements feel disconnected from the grounded family drama that makes the series so compelling. Tonally inconsistent at times.
Kaguya-sama Love is War
The funniest and smartest romantic comedy in anime history. The psychological mind games between Kaguya and Miyuki are pure comedic genius.
Kaguya-sama Love is War
Brilliant adaptation by A-1 Pictures. The narrator narrator commentary, animation gags, and character dynamics make every episode a joy to watch.
Kaguya-sama Love is War
Dual Confession arc is peak romance anime. The show manages to be hilarious while delivering incredibly sweet and genuine emotional progression.
Kaguya-sama Love is War
Chika Fujiwara and Ishigami add so much comedic value. Ishigami character arc in season two is surprisingly emotional and grounded.
Kaguya-sama Love is War
A masterpiece of rom-com storytelling. It parodies psychological thrillers like Death Note while building a deeply heartwarming romance.
